2027-07-05.title: Monday of the Fourteenth Week in Ordinary Time
readings: How awesome is this place! This is none other than the house of God
My God, in whom I trust
If I only touch his cloak, I will be made well
2027-07-05.alt: Weekday of Ordinary Time, Week 14 (Year I). From today the first readings turn to the stories of Jacob and Joseph in Genesis, which will be read through the week. Optional memorial of St Anthony Zaccaria, priest. The proper readings from the Common of Pastors may be used. Liturgical colour: green (white for the memorial).
2027-07-05.verse: Then Jacob woke from his sleep and said, “Surely the Lord is in this place—and I did not know it!” And he was afraid, and said, “How awesome is this place! This is none other than the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven.”
theo: Jacob is alone. He has cheated his brother Esau of his blessing and has to run for his life, a man with a staff, a bag and a guilty conscience, walking from Beer-sheba toward Haran, a journey of some five hundred miles. When the sun sets, he stops at “a certain place,” and the Bible does not even name it. He takes “one of the stones of the place” and puts it under his head, and falls asleep. Then he dreams: “there was a ladder set up on the earth, the top of it reaching to heaven; and the angels of God were ascending and descending on it.” And above it stands the Lord himself, who does not scold the runaway but renews the promises made to Abraham and Isaac: the land, a great family, a blessing for all the families of the earth, and then the sentence that Jacob most needs: “Know that I am with you and will keep you wherever you go, and will bring you back to this land; for I will not leave you until I have done what I have promised you.” Jacob wakes up and says one of the best-known sentences of the Book of Genesis: “Surely the Lord is in this place—and I did not know it!” The cold roadside is the “house of God” and the “gate of heaven.” He sets up the stone as a pillar, pours oil on it, and names the place Bethel, “house of God.” Then he makes a vow, still a bargain, as if God had to prove himself: “If God will be with me ... then the Lord shall be my God.” But the God who gave the promise is patient, and will teach Jacob over the years. The Church uses this very text when she dedicates a church: “This is none other than the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven” (Catechism 1180–1181). The Psalm answers Jacob's night: “You who live in the shelter of the Most High ... will say to the Lord, ‘My refuge and my fortress; my God, in whom I trust.’”

Matthew compresses two healings into one chapter and weaves them together, and the woman's story is placed inside the ruler's. A leader of the synagogue, whose name Mark and Luke give as Jairus, kneels before Jesus: “My daughter has just died; but come and lay your hand on her, and she will live.” This father has no promise to rely on, only a hope. Jesus gets up and follows him. On the road a woman who has had a flow of blood for twelve years comes up behind and touches the fringe of his cloak, one of the tassels that a Jewish man wore by the commandment of the Law. She does not dare to speak; she is ritually unclean, and she does not want to make Jesus unclean. “If I only touch his cloak, I will be made well.” Jesus turns and sees her, and says a tender word: “Take heart, daughter; your faith has made you well.” With that word the nameless woman is received into the family. Then they reach the house. The flute players and the crowd making a commotion are the professional mourners of the day. Jesus says: “Go away; for the girl is not dead but sleeping.” And they laughed at him. When the crowd has been put outside, he goes in and takes her by the hand, and the girl gets up. Jacob learned in the night that the Lord is with him wherever he goes. The ruler and the woman learn that the Lord is with them in the street, in their trouble. And we learn the same on St Anthony Zaccaria's day: this physician from Cremona, who became a priest at twenty-six, knew that a person's deepest sickness is not of the body, and he spent his short life, only thirty-six years, healing souls.
outline: Ask: when did you last feel completely alone, and where did you meet God unexpectedly?
Point 1 · Surely the Lord is in this place
Jacob, a runaway, sleeps on a stone and finds the gate of heaven.
The promise on the road: God stays with the wanderer until his word is done.
A ruler and an unclean woman both reach Jesus, one by asking and one by touching.
A physician who became a priest and treated the sickness of souls.
“Know that I am with you and will keep you wherever you go.”
live: Several times today, in your workplace, on a bus or in the kitchen, whisper: Surely the Lord is in this place. Look for him there.
At the next Mass, make a conscious act of faith as you receive Communion: if I only touch him, I will be made well.
saints: Born in Cremona in northern Italy; his father died when he was young, and his mother Antonia devoted herself to him. He studied medicine at Padua and practised as a physician in Cremona, then was ordained priest in 1528. In Milan he founded, with two friends, the Clerics Regular of St Paul, later called Barnabites after the church of St Barnabas in Milan, which they received some years after his death. He also helped to found the Angelic Sisters of St Paul and a lay group, the Married of St Paul. He loved the letters of St Paul, promoted devotion to the Eucharist, especially the Forty Hours, and preached missions to renew parish life. He died at Cremona on 5 July 1539, aged thirty-six. Canonised in 1897.
2027-07-05.prayer: God of Jacob, who met a runaway on the road and promised never to leave him, we thank you that you are in this place and in every place where we walk. Give us eyes to see the gate of heaven in the ordinary. Lord Jesus, who took the daughter of the ruler by the hand and called the woman who touched your cloak your daughter, take us by the hand when we are afraid, and let our faith touch you. Through the intercession of St Anthony Zaccaria, physician of body and soul, heal what is sick in us and in your Church, and make us eager to live by the word of St Paul. Amen.
altar: Jacob called the place of his dream Bethel and said, This is none other than the house of God. Every church in which the Eucharist is celebrated is a Bethel: the altar is the stone on which the Lord offers himself, and the Eucharist is the ladder on which heaven comes down to earth and earth rises to heaven. The woman touched the fringe of his cloak and was healed; at Communion we receive not the fringe but the Lord himself. St Anthony Zaccaria taught his Barnabites to keep the Forty Hours of adoration before the Blessed Sacrament, in which the Lord is truly the God who says, I am with you.

quick: Jacob flees from Esau, sleeps on a stone and dreams of a ladder to heaven; the Lord promises to be with him wherever he goes.
Jacob wakes and says: Surely the Lord is in this place; he sets up the stone as a pillar and calls the place Bethel.
A synagogue leader asks Jesus to raise his dead daughter; on the way a woman is healed by touching his cloak; Jesus takes the girl by the hand and she rises.
2027-07-05.action: Say Surely the Lord is in this place, quietly, three times today.
2027-07-05.question: Where in my ordinary life could God be present, and I did not know it?
kidsaint: Anthony was a boy in Italy whose father died when he was little, and his mother taught him to love the poor. He became a doctor, because he wanted to help sick people. But he saw that many people were sick in a different way: they had forgotten God. So he became a priest, and with his friends he started a group called the Barnabites. They went through towns talking about Jesus and taking care of people. Anthony loved to read the letters of St Paul. He died when he was only thirty-six. Lesson: we can help people's bodies and hearts, and we can lead them to Jesus.

family.explain: Jacob was alone and afraid. He lay down on the ground with a stone as his pillow and fell asleep. In his dream he saw a ladder going up to heaven, and angels climbing up and down. God said: I am with you. When Jacob woke up, he said: surely God is in this place, and I did not know it! In the Gospel, a woman touched the edge of Jesus' cloak and was healed, and Jesus took a little girl by the hand and she got up.
family.intention: We thank God that he is with us wherever we are, at home, at school, on the road. We pray for children who are frightened or far from home.
family.ask: Ask: “When were we afraid, and God was with us?”

illus: A young man from a village in Pathanamthitta left for work in the Gulf, and spent his first night in a crowded labour camp, with his bag under his head. He had never been so far from his mother. She had pressed a small crucifix into his hand at the airport. In the middle of the night, hearing the snoring of forty strangers and the roar of the air-conditioner, he took the crucifix out, held it and said, almost without thinking: Lord, you are in this place too. He told his parish priest, years later, that he did not feel an angel, only that he fell asleep at once. And that when he woke, the camp looked different: not a prison, but a place where he could pray. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: God of Jacob, you are with us wherever we go. Lord Jesus, we touch the fringe of your cloak with faith. Amen.
share: I did not know it! (Genesis 28:16). Where has God been present in my life without my knowing?
I am with you and will keep you wherever you go (Genesis 28:15). What fear does this promise answer?
If I only touch his cloak (Matthew 9:21). What do I bring to Jesus with the faith of this woman?
pm.resp: My God, in whom I trust.
interc: For those who are far from home, migrant workers, students and refugees.
For the sick who touch the Lord's cloak in faith through prayer and the sacraments.
For doctors, nurses and all who heal.
For priests and religious in the spirit of St Anthony Zaccaria.
For our group, that we may see God in ordinary places.
pm.close: Father, you are in this place and in every place. Keep us in your promise and bring us home. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, think of Jacob on that night. He is a man on the run. He has cheated his brother, he has left his father's house, he is going to a place he does not know. When the sun sets, he does not even have a bed. He puts a stone under his head. We all know what it is to be at a low point, alone, ashamed, unsure of the future. And that is where God meets him. In a dream he sees a ladder, and angels going up and down, and the Lord standing beside him. And what does God say? Not a scolding. He says: Know that I am with you and will keep you wherever you go (Genesis 28:15).

When Jacob wakes he says one of the great lines of the Bible: Surely the Lord is in this place, and I did not know it! (Genesis 28:16). How many times has God been in our place, in the hospital room, in the bus, in the kitchen, in the dark, and we did not know it? Today's reading invites us to open our eyes. The stone that was a pillow becomes a pillar. The roadside becomes the gate of heaven. And centuries later Jesus tells Nathanael: you will see heaven opened and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of Man (John 1:51). Jesus himself is the ladder: God and man in one person. In him heaven has come down.

In the Gospel we meet two people who need that ladder. A ruler of the synagogue: his daughter has just died, and he comes to Jesus with nothing but a request. And a woman, who has suffered for twelve years, who is afraid to speak: she touches the fringe of his cloak. And Jesus turns and sees her. Take heart, daughter; your faith has made you well (Matthew 9:22). Perhaps nobody had spoken so tenderly to her in twelve years. Then he comes to the ruler's house, where the flute players are already playing. The girl is not dead but sleeping. And they laughed at him. He takes her by the hand, and she gets up (Matthew 9:24–25).

Dear friends, if you are at a low point today, if you are far from home or from God, remember Jacob's stone. The Lord is in this place. And remember the fringe of the cloak: you do not need great words, only a touch of faith. Today the Church remembers St Anthony Zaccaria, a doctor who became a priest because he saw that souls too need a physician. May he help us to notice the sickness of the heart, in us and around us, and to bring it to the one who takes us by the hand.
kids: Children, Jacob was far from home, and it was night, and he was afraid. He lay down with a stone for a pillow. In his dream he saw a ladder up to heaven, and God said: I am with you wherever you go! When Jacob woke up he said: God is here, and I did not know it! In the Gospel a girl was very sick, and Jesus took her by the hand and made her well. Jesus is with us too, when we are at home and when we are far away. Today we remember St Anthony Zaccaria, a doctor who became a priest to help people love Jesus.

intro: Theme: “Know that I am with you and will keep you wherever you go.”
Jacob's stone at Bethel, the Lord who walks beside the runaway, and the touch of faith that reaches the hem of his cloak.

points.h: Surely the Lord is in this place
sub: A runaway with a stone for a pillow.
q: Then Jacob woke from his sleep and said, “Surely the Lord is in this place—and I did not know it!”
Very truly, I tell you, you will see heaven opened and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of Man.
points.apply: Three times today, in a place you do not think of as holy, say: Surely the Lord is in this place.

sub: Not until I have done what I have promised.
With you always, to the end of the age.
q: Know that I am with you and will keep you wherever you go, and will bring you back to this land; for I will not leave you until I have done what I have promised you.
And remember, I am with you always, to the end of the age.
points.apply: If you are far from home or from loved ones, say this promise aloud before you sleep each night this week.

sub: A father with nothing but a request.
A woman who dared only to touch.
The Lord who turns and sees.
q: he will cover you with his pinions, and under his wings you will find refuge; his faithfulness is a shield and buckler.
Jesus turned, and seeing her he said, “Take heart, daughter; your faith has made you well.”
points.apply: At each Communion this week, make a conscious act of faith: if I only touch him, I will be made well.

concl: God meets the runaway Jacob on a stone, promises to be with him wherever he goes, and makes the roadside the gate of heaven.
Jesus meets a father and a woman in need, honours the faith of the one who only touches his cloak, and takes the dead girl by the hand.
2027-07-05.resolve: Look for the Lord in the ordinary places you pass through today, and bring one fear to him in prayer.
